questions.stem: Why does potassium (atomic number 19) have the electron configuration 2, 8, 8, 1 rather than 2, 8, 9?

options.text: Because the third shell can only hold 8 electrons for elements 1-20
Because the fourth shell must fill before the third
Because potassium is a metal and metals always have 1 outer electron
Because potassium has fewer electrons than expected

questions.explanation: For the first 20 elements, the third electron shell holds a maximum of 8 electrons. Once it is full, additional electrons go into the fourth shell. So potassium's 19th electron enters the fourth shell, giving 2, 8, 8, 1.
